clue.text: Consort damaged Berlin carpet

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal husband has ruined a carpet bought in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the twelve letters of BERLIN and CARPET. Queen Victoria's husband was German-born, which makes 'Berlin' a fitting hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's husband was the royal consort, the spouse of a reigning monarch.

clue.text: Egyptian leader elevates me for one

indicators.note: 'me for one' says the word me takes the place of the word one in what precedes

parts.note: to elevate is to raise, so 'elevates' gives raises
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pharaoh lifts the speaker up, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' looks like 'for example', but it means ME stands in for one (I): RAISES becomes RA-ME-SES.
explanation.definitionFit: Several pharaohs of ancient Egypt bore this name, the most famous being the second.

clue.text: Some finer details will satisfy obsessive type

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fussy detail pleases a pedant who loves precision.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is fiNER Details. The definition is the whole phrase 'obsessive type' with 'will satisfy' read as the link between wordplay and definition only loosely; the obsessive type is the person satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: A geek fixated on one narrow interest is the kind of obsessive person who relishes fine detail.

clue.text: Scientist in nineties, befuddled

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters of nineties are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist in his nineties has become confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only the link; 'befuddled' rearranges the eight letters of NINETIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist behind relativity is the archetypal scientist.

clue.text: See 1
Plant article about spies

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ca, for circa, means about
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A news article covers espionage, and someone wants to plant it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle and mimosa trees belong to this genus of shrubs and trees.

clue.text: Bet bridal arrangement provides food for chats?

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of bet and bridal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager on the wedding plans pays for refreshments over gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chats' are not conversations but small songbirds, such as the stonechat; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform in a garden where seed and scraps are set out for small birds to feed.

clue.text: Ruling, full of potential, with no little power

indicators.note: with no says a piece is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: pregnant can mean full of possibility, as in a pregnant pause
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A ruler's position is full of promise but carries little real power.
explanation.definitionFit: A regnant monarch is one who reigns in their own right, as in queen regnant.

clue.text: Notes recalled European capital toured by chap with American lawyer

indicators.note: a place toured by someone is gone round by them, so the man goes around the capital

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: recalled read as called back says the capital's letters run backwards

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: Notes recall a European capital visited by a man with his American lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembered, but it means called back, so the capital is read backwards before the chap goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written reminders, the plural of memorandum.

clue.text: Military man with strategy over alien from Jupiter, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it stands above it

parts.note: a major is an army officer
a plan is a strategy
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An army officer plans for an alien coming from Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is the largest of the eight principal bodies orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: Correct equipment starts to help team

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as on an oil rig

indicators.note: the starts of the two following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The right kit is the start of helping a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms, as in the correct answer.

clue.text: Doctor attending to problems on plane?

definitions.text: Doctor attending to problems on plane?

parts.words: Doctor attending to problems on plane?
parts.note: the plane is the plane tree, not an aircraft, and the doctor treats diseased trees

explanation.surface: A physician helps a passenger taken ill in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who treats damaged or diseased trees is jocularly called a doctor of them.

clue.text: Make fun of boy forgetting name around start of school

indicators.note: around says the shortened name goes about the next piece
forgetting something means leaving it out, so the name letter is dropped

parts.note: John is a common boy's name

indicators.note: the start of school is its first letter

explanation.surface: Tease a boy who forgot his name as he started school.
explanation.walkthrough: JOHN loses N to give JOH, which goes around S: JO-S-H.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh is to tease or banter good-humouredly.

clue.text: Feature of stag-night excursion with drinks in South-East

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A stag party's excursion includes drinks in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag night is a British groom's party with his friends before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic dancer's act is a staple entertainment of bachelor parties.

clue.text: Almost reckless to install sinister religious figure

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: rash means reckless
to install is to put in

explanation.surface: It is nearly reckless to appoint a dark holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian mystic who held sway over the last Tsar's family is remembered as a malign monk-like figure.

clue.text: Alien hunter, upper-class fool, confused point at issue

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters of fool are scrambled

parts.note: the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: An upper-class fool hunts for aliens, muddling the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies reported flying saucers is in effect a seeker of extraterrestrials.

clue.text: Crazy about hot spas

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about hot springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Public bathing places with mineral or hot water are called spas.

clue.text: Girls are heartlessly playing with love in harem

indicators.note: playing suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged
heartlessly removes the middle of are, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Girls are cruelly toying with love in a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves A and E from ARE; 'playing' rearranges GIRLS with AE to make SERAGLI, then O.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim household, as in the Ottoman palace.

clue.text: Look to ensnare beast of burden with rope

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap inside, so one piece closes around the other

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
an ass is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to catch a donkey with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope used for catching cattle, and to lasso is to rope one.

clue.text: Find a home around a US city

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes about the second

parts.note: to settle is to make a home somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a place to live around an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State.

clue.text: One chooses first two of eleven in division

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the division

parts.note: a sector is a division

indicators.note: the first two of a word are its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A team picker selects the first two players of the eleven in a division.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team is an eleven, which fits the selector of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks players for a national team, so is the one who chooses.

clue.text: Cheat, spelled with a double T?

definitions.meaning: to cheat on a partner is to be unfaithful
a double T is the letter T written twice, that is on two occasions

explanation.definitionFit: Being unfaithful to a lover is two-timing; a doubled letter appears on two occasions.

clue.text: Crossword fan, nothing less, accepting one class of medal

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shortened word goes around the next piece
less means minus, so the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: a crossword fan is a solver
nothing is zero, the letter O
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A puzzle enthusiast, after a near miss, accepts second place in the medals.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLVER loses O to give SLVER, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Second place in a competition earns the medal of this metal, between gold and bronze.

clue.text: The type of Italian one's dying to meet?

definitions.text: The type of Italian one's dying to meet?

parts.words: The type of Italian one's dying to meet?
parts.note: the saying 'see Naples and die' makes a native of that city the Italian one dies after meeting

explanation.surface: Which sort of Italian is everyone longing to be introduced to?
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, the city of the saying about seeing it and dying.

clue.text: Against entering garden in Sussex town

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hoe is to work in the garden
v is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to it walks into a garden in a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton in East Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is a resort on the English south coast, now part of the city of Brighton and Hove.

clue.text: Deal with thirst, despatching second quantity of water

indicators.note: despatching means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to slake thirst is to quench it

explanation.surface: To quench a thirst, someone quickly sends off for some water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is a large body of water surrounded by land.

clue.text: Unison passage: critical comment rejected it

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of disapproval

indicators.note: rejected read as thrown back says the letters of it run backwards

explanation.surface: A critic dismissed a passage sung in unison.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all performers to play together.

clue.text: Crude fellow, very East European, not British

indicators.note: not says a letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a Bulgarian is from eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A coarse man, very much an East European, is not from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East European' looks like a description of the fellow, but it supplies the nationality that loses its British letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse, ill-mannered person, often one flaunting new wealth.

clue.text: Paper knife possibly used in salutation?

definitions.meaning: the greeting at the start of a ..., such as 'Dear Sir', opens it

explanation.definitionFit: A blade for slitting envelopes, and also the first words of a piece of correspondence.

clue.text: See 27
